meta.route: Node, @poe2/core analyzeCharacter with raw data fetched live via the ninja proxy (https://poe2-v3-ninja-proxy.vercel.app). Options match apps/web/src/app/character/page.tsx: tiers (mod-tiers.json), tree (passive-tree.json), ladder (fetchLadder via proxy, league + ascendancy). Panel-derived sections (damage review, gear targets, audit, tree allocation, headroom) computed with the same core calls the components use. Not a browser render.
notIncluded: analysis.model (raw poe.ninja payload echo, ~490 KB; fetch it from the proxy to reproduce)
mod-display.json (not in packages/data/generated; only affects text of implicit/unique mods, shown as raw ids on a few jewel mods)
Progress history, Compare, Chat (browser localStorage / LLM; no state in a headless run)

recommendations.action: Toughen up against physical hits — a 4,399 physical hit kills you first.
recommendations.rationale: Physical is your weakest defence, so it's what kills you first.
recommendations.detail: Physical has the lowest maximum survivable hit of any damage type that can kill this character, 4.3x below the strongest. The figure opposite is the CEILING — what this vector would reach if it matched the safest one.

impact.label: Lowest maximum hit taken — ceiling if fully closed

cost.detail: Add maximum life, energy shield, or physical-specific mitigation.

evidence.note: A single physical hit of 4,399 kills. Your toughest type (cold) survives 19,126 — 4.3x more.
Effective health pool reads 18,456, overstating the true one-shot threshold by 4.2x. Do not use it to judge this build's safety.

recommendations.action: Swap a suffix on Mind Spur for "of Bameth" — it replaces +(36-40)% to Cold Resistance (tier 1, 24-27% chaos resistance). This is one line, so it is one choice: "of Bameth" (tier 1, 24-27% chaos resistance): closes 6 of the 6% chaos shortfall; or "of Ephij" (tier 1, 41-45% lightning resistance): closes 2 of the 2% lightning shortfall.
recommendations.rationale: A cheap way to close your chaos resistance gap.
recommendations.detail: Cold resistance is 59% above the cap, and this mod grants 36%. At least 36% of it is doing nothing. 1 swap of this kind covers the 6% chaos shortfall; 4 are available.

cost.detail: Recrafting one suffix on Mind Spur. The rest of each item is unaffected.

recommendations.tradeoff: Gives up +(36-40)% to Cold Resistance on Mind Spur. That is already partly wasted, so the loss is smaller than the number suggests — but it is not zero if you later lose another source of it.

evidence.note: chaos resistance is 6% below the cap.
Cold resistance is 59% above the cap, and this mod grants 36%. At least 36% of it is doing nothing.
"of Bameth" is tier 1 and rolls 24-27% on this base at item level 81.
The same line could instead close 2 of the 2% lightning shortfall.

recommendations.action: Fill the 1 empty affix slot on your gear — start with Demon Pendant, which has 1 suffix unused.
recommendations.rationale: Empty affix slots give nothing. Filling them is a safe upgrade whatever your build.
recommendations.detail: 5 active items carry 29 of a possible 30 affixes, with 1 of them holding room. An empty slot grants nothing regardless of what this build is scaling, so unlike a low-tier modifier it is worth filling whatever direction the character takes.

cost.detail: An augment per slot, on an item that keeps everything already on it. 1 such slot is available; each is worth doing on its own.

recommendations.tradeoff: An added modifier is a rolled modifier — it cannot be chosen outright, and it spends the slot that a later, better roll would have wanted.

evidence.note: Demon Pendant (Rare, item level 79) has 1 suffix unused.
2 items (Mind Keep, Behemoth Band) carry modifiers the affix data cannot classify, so their used slots cannot be counted and they are left out of this total entirely.

headroomReport.summary: Against BASE monsters this character has 13.2x headroom at tier 16, the highest waystone. Rares, uniques and map mods hit harder and are not modelled here.
caveats: Measured against a BASE monster of that area level. Rares, uniques and map mods hit much harder and are not modelled, so treat this as an upper bound, not a safety verdict.
Headroom is against physical damage, the type that kills this character soonest. Other damage types have more room.
Base monster damage is physical. A character whose weakest defence is elemental or chaos has less real headroom than the physical figure suggests.
Comfortable means surviving 12 base hits or more; dangerous means fewer than 6. Those thresholds are this project's judgement, not a game constant.

unresolved.question: How much harder does a specific rare, unique or map modifier hit?
unresolved.missing: Monster damage multipliers per rarity and per map modifier are not in the data used here. Only the base monster figure for the area level is derived, so rare, unique and boss hits are not scored.
